verses.text: After these things, King Xerxes promoted Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite. He gave him a higher position than all the other officials.
All the king's officials at the king's gate bowed down and honored Haman, because the king had ordered it. But Mordecai would not bow down or honor him.
The king's officials at the gate asked Mordecai, "Why do you disobey the king's order?"
Day after day they spoke to him, but he would not listen. So they told Haman about it, to see whether Mordecai's reason would be accepted, because he had told them he was a Jew.
When Haman saw that Mordecai would not bow down or honor him, he was furious.
But he did not want to punish only Mordecai. He had been told who Mordecai's people were. So Haman looked for a way to destroy all of Mordecai's people, the Jews, all through the kingdom of Xerxes.

In the first month, the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Xerxes, they threw the pur, which means the lot, in front of Haman, to choose a day and a month. The lot fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar.

Then Haman said to King Xerxes, "There is a certain people scattered among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom. Their customs are different from everyone else's, and they do not obey the king's laws. It is not good for the king to let them live.
If it pleases the king, let an order be written to destroy them. I will pay about three hundred forty tonnes of silver to the men in charge of the king's business, to put into the royal treasury."
So the king took his signet ring off his finger and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.
The king said to Haman, "Keep the money, and do whatever you want with the people."

On the thirteenth day of the first month, the king's secretaries were called. They wrote down all of Haman's orders to the king's governors, to the rulers of each province, and to the officials of each people. They wrote to each province in its own writing and to each people in their own language. It was written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with the king's ring.

Messengers took the letters to all the king's provinces. The orders were to destroy, kill, and wipe out all the Jews, young and old, little children and women, on a single day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and to take everything they owned.
A copy of the order was to be made law in every province and announced to all the peoples, so they would be ready for that day.
At the king's command, the messengers hurried out, and the order was announced in the fortress city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Susa was confused and upset.
